title: Lower bound for fibres of an irreducible finite-type scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be an irreducible scheme [def-weil-irreducible-components] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. There exists a natural number $r$ such that
$$\dim X=\dim\overline{f(X)}+r,$$
where dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and the natural number is embedded in the extended dimension type. For every $x\in X$, the local topological dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_{f(x)}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(f(x))$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] at the point corresponding to $x$ is at least $r$. Moreover, the locus of points where this local fibre dimension equals $r$ is dense open in $X$.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, parts (2)(a) and (2)(b), including the proof via the generic point and the transcendence-degree difference

proof.text: First check finiteness for the fibre calculations. A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, generated by $0$ and $1$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a one-point quasi-compact scheme. The finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem makes $X$ Noetherian. The minimal-closed-subset theorem gives the descending-chain condition on closed subsets of $|X|$: an infinite strictly descending chain would have no minimal member. The compact-subsets theorem therefore makes every subset of $|X|$ quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, preliminary finite-type fibre assertion; auxiliary Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01OZ (properties-lemma-Noetherian-topology), 04ZA (topology-lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Write $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure maps. Since $a_X=a_Y\circ f$ is locally of finite type, clause (f) of the permanence theorem shows that $f$ is locally of finite type. For every affine open $V\subseteq Y$, its inverse image is a subset of $|X|$, hence is quasi-compact by Step 1. Thus $f$ is quasi-compact and therefore finite type by definition. For every $y\in Y$, finite-type base change now makes the fibre projection $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ finite type. In particular all these fibre schemes have finite topological dimension, by the finite-type-over-a-field dimension theorem.

source.place: Tag 0B2L (1) and its proof; Tags 01T8 (lemma-permanence-finite-type), 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type); finite-dimensionality over a field.

proof.text: Irreducibility includes nonemptiness. By sobriety choose the generic point $\eta$ of $X$, and put $\xi=f(\eta)$. The closed subset $f^{-1}(\overline{\{\xi\}})$ contains $\eta$, hence all of $X$. Thus $f(X)\subseteq\overline{\{\xi\}}$, while $\xi\in f(X)$ gives the reverse inclusion after taking closures. Consequently $Z=\overline{\{\xi\}}$ is a nonempty irreducible closed subset of $Y$, with generic point $\xi$. Every nonempty open subset of $X$ contains $\eta$: otherwise its closed complement would contain $\eta$ and hence $X$.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, proof of (2), first two sentences; sobriety Tag 01IS (schemes-lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text:
Apply the closed-irreducible dimension/transcendence-degree theorem to $X\subseteq X$ with generic point $\eta$, and to $Z\subseteq Y$ with generic point $\xi$. Both ambient schemes are finite type over $k$, and both closed subsets are nonempty irreducible by Step 3. It gives $\dim X=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_X(\eta)$ and $\dim Z=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_Y(\xi)$. These are finite nonnegative integers: $X$ and $Y$ have finite dimension by the finite-type dimension theorem, and a chain in the closed subspace $Z$ is also a chain in $Y$. The residue-field map of $f$ gives a tower $k\to\kappa_Y(\xi)\to\kappa_X(\eta)$. The transcendence-degree tower identity therefore yields
$$\dim X=\dim Z+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa_Y(\xi)}\kappa_X(\eta),$$
so choose $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa_Y(\xi)}\kappa_X(\eta)\in\mathbb N$.
Finiteness of $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa_X(\eta)$ makes both summands in that tower identity finite, so this is ordinary integer subtraction without any infinite-dimension ambiguity.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, proof of (2), displayed transcendence-degree difference; Tag 0B1C (item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg in lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), Fields Tag 030H (lemma-transcendence-degree-tower).

proof.text:
Put $F=X_\xi$, and let $\widetilde\eta\in F$ correspond to $\eta$. The fibre homeomorphism identifies $|F|$ with the subspace $f^{-1}(\xi)$ containing $\eta$. The closure of $\eta$ in this subspace is $\overline{\{\eta\}}\cap f^{-1}(\xi)=f^{-1}(\xi)$, so $F$ is nonempty irreducible with generic point $\widetilde\eta$. Its residue field is $\kappa_X(\eta)$ as an extension of $\kappa_Y(\xi)$, as follows directly from the fibre-product residue-field theorem. Indeed the tensor ring for this fibre-product point is
$$\kappa_X(\eta)\otimes_{\kappa_Y(\xi)}\kappa_Y(\xi)\simeq\kappa_X(\eta),\qquad a\otimes b\longmapsto a f^\sharp(b),$$
with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. This is a field; the unital map from it to $\kappa_F(\widetilde\eta)$ has zero kernel. The theorem identifies the latter residue field with the residue field at that zero prime, namely this same field, compatibly with both factor maps.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, proof of (2), generic fibre at the image of the generic point; Tag 01JT (schemes-lemma-points-fibre-product), residue-field clause.

proof.text:
The scheme $F$ is finite type over $\kappa_Y(\xi)$ by Step 2 and irreducible with generic point $\widetilde\eta$ by Step 5. Apply the closed-irreducible dimension theorem to its whole underlying space. By the compatible residue-field identification of Step 5 and Step 4,
$$\dim F=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa_Y(\xi)}\kappa_F(\widetilde\eta)=r.$$
The irreducible locally-algebraic dimension theorem applies to $F$ over this field, since finite type implies locally finite type. It says that dimension at every point equals the global dimension. In particular $\dim_{\widetilde\eta}F=r$. No reducedness, smoothness or dominance onto $Y$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, proof of (2), final equality of the displayed calculation; Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), parts (3), (6).

proof.text:
Fix $x\in X$, and let $\widetilde x\in X_{f(x)}$ be its corresponding fibre point. By Step 2 the global dimension of this nonempty fibre is finite. The minimum defining its dimension at $\widetilde x$ is therefore a finite nonnegative integer $n$, bounded above by the dimension of the whole fibre, which is itself an open neighbourhood. Apply openness of the local fibre-dimension bound to the locally finite type morphism $f$ and this integer $n$. Its open set
$$U_n=\{z\in X:\dim_{\widetilde z}X_{f(z)}\leq n\}$$
contains $x$, hence is nonempty and contains $\eta$ by Step 3. Evaluation at $\eta$ and Step 6 give $r=\dim_{\widetilde\eta}X_\xi\leq n=\dim_{\widetilde x}X_{f(x)}$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, this proves the lower bound everywhere.

Use the same openness theorem with the nonnegative integer $r$ of Step 4. It makes $U_r$ open, and Step 6 shows that $\eta\in U_r$. Since $\overline{\{\eta\}}=X$, this open set is dense. By Step 7 every local fibre dimension is at least $r$, so the condition defining $U_r$ is equivalent to equality with $r$. Therefore the entire equality locus, not merely a subset of it, is dense open in $X$.
